actual_scope: The non-complement two-pair exchange for the six-source weight-3 count at characteristic 7, under the inherited centre-only free-type hypothesis. The question is whether (10, 14) and (11, 13) can both be new when (9, 15) is not weight 3 and push the cover to 20. This package shows both can be new and that the cover is then exactly 3. The complement subcase has cover 4 and is the three-new window of PR #7032. Unrestricted c=7 existence stays open.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one new connector operation. This package keeps the unsigned dirty connector alphabet fixed and answers open question 1 of the two-pair census in PR #7032: the joint walks whose (9, 15) sum is not a complement. A new operation is not the missing step.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the recursive-interface schedule. It does not change a supplier, a consumer, or kappa. It bounds the non-complement two-pair replacement inside the weight-3 count at c=7 and leaves the full depth-two question open.
stop_rule: Stop once every centre-only chain on which (10, 14) and (11, 13) are both weight 3 is classified, or stop if one non-complement chain has weight-3 cover 20.
evidence: Exhaustive free-type census. Both pairs are weight 3 only for 720 joined shapes of one common mask. The prefix s=4..10 and the tail s=14..21 are frozen on that mask, and s=12 carries either the same mask or the (11, 13) mask. (0, 3) and (33, 33) add nothing. (9, 15) adds the complement only on the complement endpoints. The non-complement cover is exactly 3, attained by 576 windows per mask and by one explicit word. The complement cover is exactly 4, attained by the 72 three-new windows of PR #7032 and by its word. A forward count and a backward count agree on 7818720 shared-mask paths from s=10 to s=14; only 2160 of them make both sums weight 3. A one-letter mutation is rejected.

open_questions.question: On a centre-only chain where s=10 and s=14 share a mask, s=11 and s=13 share a different mask, and exactly one of those two sums is weight 3, what is the weight-3 cover?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Both sums being weight 3 forces the masks to agree and drops the cover to 3 or 4. A shared-mask walk with only one new pair is the remaining way the 7818720 paths could approach a large cover. Separate endpoint equalities still suggest an image of size at most 16 and a cover of at most 19, and that counting is not proved here.
open_questions.first_step: Fix the weight-3 end to one of the 180 shapes and enumerate the states at the other pair whose common mask is different.
open_questions.blocked_by: Those paths are outside the 2160 both-shape paths classified here.
